justification: Both publish guards read only the old row shape. The AI reader puts the clause title in section_header and the number in ref_number, and zones come from the chapter config at enrichment, so the Campbelltown Part 3 re-read (every section and zone kept) was refused by both and needed hand overrides; 18 more chapters would need the same. section-loss now falls back to the code in ref_number; area-link counts precinct/marker links and zone-only links apart and predicts config_specific zones with the tagger enrichment runs. Live read-only: Campbelltown Part 3 105 codes (old 109; 3 lost are line labels) and 547 zoned vs 504 before. Also: dcp_extract_changed now re-derives precinct keys after publish via the shared rederive_after_publish (KRG 14A/14H went live with 0 keyed rows on 2026-10-18), and KRG 14C is listed not-covered by whole chapter (expect 80) since the re-read replaced its row ids; DQ-146 0.

falsifiable_check.command: python -m pytest -q -o addopts= tests/test_dcp_area_link_guard.py tests/test_dcp_supersede_guard.py tests/test_dcp_commit_refuses_section_loss.py tests/test_dcp_legibility_guard.py tests/test_dcp_commit_approved_records_hash.py
falsifiable_check.fails_when: the ref fallback is removed or outranks the header, prose zones are counted as config zones, the two link kinds are pooled, or config zones are not predicted
falsifiable_check.observed_red: Each of those five mutations failed exactly one test; restored, all pass.

real_layer_exempt.scripts/dcp_area_link_guard.py: PYTEST_REAL_DB area-link test passes; live Campbelltown Part 3 Linked(0,504) -> predicted Linked(0,547), read-only
real_layer_exempt.scripts/dcp_supersede_guard.py: live Campbelltown Part 3 snapshot 105 codes, read-only
real_layer_exempt.scripts/dcp_extract_changed.py: call site only; the derivation it calls was run live for ku_ring_gai (dry run 1,637 rows already keyed)
real_layer_exempt.scripts/dcp_commit_approved.py: block moved into the shared function; commit re-derive suite passes unchanged

pre_impl.existing_data: Campbelltown Part 3 live rows: section_header is a title or empty, ref_number '<doc>__3_7_1_2 d)'; superseded rows carry '3.7.1.6 iv) ...' in section_header
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: guards assumed the code is in section_header and that zone links come only from precinct/gate rules
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: extends both existing guards; same call sites and override flags

functions.name: ref_code
functions.input: one ref_number string, possibly NULL or old-shape
functions.output: section code after the last '__', underscores read as dots
functions.if_none: None, and the row adds no code

functions.name: config_zoned_ids
functions.input: cursor plus council and chapter key of the uncommitted version
functions.output: ids enrichment will give a config_specific zone limit
functions.if_none: empty set (tagger import failure) -> fewer links predicted -> refuses

functions.name: rederive_after_publish
functions.input: the set of councils this run published, and dry_run
functions.output: precinct keys re-derived per council; warnings on failure
functions.if_none: no council or dry run: nothing runs

queries.purpose: count live area links before the swap, precinct/marker and zone-only apart
read every current row's header and ref to collect section codes
queries.where_clause: source_council = %s AND source_chapter_key = %s AND is_current = TRUE

break_it.scenario: a chapter loses its precinct links but every row gets config zones
break_it.what_happens: the publish is refused and rolled back

break_it.scenario: zones read from a rule's own prose
break_it.what_happens: those rows are not counted as re-linkable

break_it.scenario: new refs carry no code either
break_it.what_happens: still refused as a section loss
break_it.how: fallback only adds codes it can parse

break_it.scenario: the derivation for one published council raises an error
break_it.what_happens: a warning names the command and the next council still runs

post_merge.db_reset: none: no schema or data change, guards only read
post_merge.manual_verify: next live re-read of a doubled-text chapter passes both guards without --allow-section-loss / --allow-area-link-loss
